longform.topic_title: How to Become a Better YouTuber: Packaging, Retention & Your First 1,000 Subs
longform.summary: Across the long-form field, packaging beats production — the videos that break out teach one repeatable system (idea, title, thumbnail, hook) instead of narrating a personal YouTube journey. Generic 'grow fast' advice is the most saturated and worst-performing shape in the set.

goals: See the highest-ceiling example in the space
Copy a format that compounds across uploads
Learn the hook that broke this creator out
hooks: Opens by naming the outcome the viewer wants, then promises the exact steps.
Leads with a specific number as proof before any advice lands.
Names the mistake the viewer is probably making right now.
Contradicts the common advice in the first line to open a curiosity gap.
Shows the result on screen first, then rewinds to how it was built.

common_features.note: Puts 'YouTube' or 'channel' directly in the title.
A specific subscriber or view figure signals proof.
Names the payoff up front ('how to …').

emotional_triggers.trigger: Fear of wasting years on the wrong thing

structure_patterns.name: "Show the analytics" (highest engagement)
structure_patterns.note: Real retention graphs and CTR screenshots beat talking-head opinion.

structure_patterns.name: One specific number, early
structure_patterns.note: A concrete result (subs gained, CTR %) in the first 30s earns the watch.

structure_patterns.name: Mistake → fix → proof
structure_patterns.note: Name what the viewer is doing wrong, show the fix, then the receipts.

what_to_avoid: Generic 'grow your channel fast' advice — it is the most saturated shape in the set.
Burying the payoff; the first 30 seconds decide retention.
Story-time about your own journey with no transferable system.

shorts.topic_title: YouTube Growth Shorts: The Creator Advice That Actually Travels
shorts.summary: In short-form, one tactic per clip wins. The Shorts that break out state a single fixable mistake in the first two seconds — multi-tip 'ultimate guide' Shorts underperform badly against their channel size.

keywords: how to grow on youtube shorts
how to get views on youtube

goals: See the highest-ceiling Short in the space
Study a single-tactic clip that travels
Copy a hook that works without sound
Learn the pattern interrupt that stops the scroll
hooks: States one fixable mistake in the first two seconds.
Opens on the result, then explains it in a single sentence.
Asks the question the viewer is already asking themselves.
Shows the before/after on screen with no preamble.

common_features.note: One idea per Short, named in the title.
Opens a curiosity gap with a question.

structure_patterns.name: One tactic, one clip (highest engagement)
structure_patterns.note: Single-idea Shorts outperform multi-tip rundowns at every channel size.

structure_patterns.name: On-screen text carries it
structure_patterns.note: The tip reads without sound — captions do the work in the feed.

structure_patterns.name: Mistake → fix, under 30 seconds
structure_patterns.note: Name it, fix it, stop. The shortest clips hold the highest completion.

what_to_avoid: Multi-tip 'ultimate guide' Shorts — they underperform at every channel size here.
Slow intros; the first two seconds decide whether the scroll stops.
Advice with no on-screen proof — it reads as recycled.
